items.markdown:
![Pad Thai - RecipeTin Eats](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07280155-1672-0139-0000-ad1a65048969:4)
Pad Thai is `a famous stir-fried rice noodle dish from Thailand made with rice noodles, eggs, tofu, and a protein like shrimp or chicken` . It features a sweet, salty, and sour sauce made from tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar, and is finished with crushed peanuts and bean sprouts.[](https://www.recipetineats.com/chicken-pad-thai/) [[1]](https://www.recipetineats.com/chicken-pad-thai/)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pad_thai)[[3]](https://www.cuisineathome.com/articles/what-is-pad-thai/)[[4]](https://thai-foodie.com/thaifood/pad-thai-the-complete-authentic-guide/)[[5]](https://mangosteenbristol.co.uk/what-is-pad-thai/)[[6]](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/pad-thai)

Core Ingredients

- **Noodles:** Flat rice stick noodles soaked until soft rather than boiled.
- **Protein:** Traditionally shrimp or prawns, though chicken, pork, or firm tofu are also very popular.
- **Aromatics & Veggies:** Garlic, shallots, garlic chives, and fresh mung bean sprouts.
- **Sauce Components:** Tamarind pulp or paste for sourness, fish sauce for saltiness, and palm sugar for sweetness.
- **Garnishes:** Lime wedges, chopped roasted peanuts, and dried chili flakes served right on the side or top.[](https://www.recipetineats.com/chicken-pad-thai/) [[1]](https://www.feastingathome.com/15-minute-pad-thai/)[[2]](https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/best-pad-thai/)[[3]](https://thaisq.com/pad-thai-what-makes-this-noodle-dish-interesting/)

History and Popularity

- **Origins:** While stir-frying techniques came to the region from China, Pad Thai was heavily promoted by the Thai government in the mid-20th century around World War II during a rice shortage to encourage alternative grain and noodle consumption.
- **National Status:** It became a recognized national dish of Thailand and a staple street food.
- **Global Reach:** It is now one of the most widely ordered items in Thai restaurants worldwide.[](https://mangosteenbristol.co.uk/what-is-pad-thai/) [[1]](https://dukelanguage.com/2013/12/pad-thai/)[[2]](https://tastesbetterfromscratch.com/pad-thai/)
